exercises.name: Incline Bench Press (Barbell)

source_english.description: Incline Bench Press (Barbell) lowers the bar to the upper chest on an inclined bench, then presses it back to lockout.
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep wrists stacked over the elbows.
Brace the trunk and keep the shoulder blades controlled.
Use a smooth lower and press.
source_english.safety_note: Use a stable setup and stop before the shoulders or wrists lose controlled alignment.

exercises.name: Incline Chest Fly (Dumbbell)

Move through a controlled arc.
Stop at a comfortable range.

exercises.name: Lunge (Barbell)

source_english.description: The barbell forward lunge steps one foot ahead, lowers both knees, then drives through the front foot to return.
instructions: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and a barbell resting on your upper back.
Take a step forward with your right foot, keeping your torso upright.
Lower your body by bending your right knee until your thigh is parallel to the ground.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat with your left leg, alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the feet planted.
Track the knees with the toes.
Keep the chest and trunk controlled.
source_english.safety_note: Use a depth and load that allow a stable knee and hip path.

style.framing: Full figure and all required equipment/supports visible within a square. Scale and use a three-quarter view to expose the specified contacts without changing anatomy, equipment, grip or technique.
style.no_invention: Technique, equipment and muscles come only from the attached exact catalogue record. No extra attachments, numerical weights, brands or exact angles absent from the source.

scene.single_phase: Upper-abdomen row endpoint from near-horizontal hinge
scene.composition: Stand shoulder-width with knees slightly bent; hip hinge leaves the straight back and torso near horizontal. Both hands grip one free barbell overhand slightly wider than shoulder width. Bar is drawn from the floor to UPPER ABDOMEN, elbows back, shoulder blades together, torso steady. Show this one top row phase, not a standing deadlift; the full source records the floor reset each repetition. Full bar and feet in frame.

source_instruction_quotes.text: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your chest up.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Pull the barbell towards your upper abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position.

prompt_payload.reference_role: Human appearance/proportions/materials only. Never copy pose, equipment or muscle targets from a reference.
